AI-First Senior PHP Developer

Avrillo | Remote (UK-based)

The short version

Avrillo is a conveyancing firm that builds its own technology. We don't bolt software onto legal processes, we rebuild how conveyancing works from the ground up, using AI as a core part of how we develop and how our platform operates.

We're looking for a Senior PHP Developer to join our established development team and help us continue transforming one of the most paper-heavy, frustrating industries in the UK.

You'll work on real systems that are live today, processing documents, verifying identities, integrating with lenders and estate agents, not prototypes or proof-of-concepts. Full AI-assisted development is already how we work. We're looking for someone who operates the same way.

What you'd actually be working on

We're mid-journey on a significant platform evolution. You'd be joining a team that's actively delivering:

  • CRM and case management rebuild — migrating away from legacy systems to something we own and control
  • AML and compliance automation — source of funds verification, identity checks, fraud detection, integrating with leading providers
  • Document intelligence — processing, extracting, and understanding legal documents at scale
  • Third-party integrations — estate agent portals, lender APIs, payment systems

This isn't theoretical. These systems handle real transactions for real clients, every day.

What "AI-driven" means here

AI isn't a line item on our roadmap, it's embedded in how we build.

We use AI-assisted development workflows as standard. We integrate LLMs and automation into the platform itself, document processing, decision support, compliance checks. If you're already working this way and have opinions about how to do it well, you'll fit right in.

The team

You'd be joining a small, close development team that owns what it builds. We're not a tech department serving "the business", we're part of the same thing. Developers here have direct input into what we build and why.

You'd work alongside teammates covering Laravel, Vue, integrations, and infrastructure. You will report to the Team Lead, who'll be your main point of contact day-to-day.

What we're looking for

Technically:

  • Production experience in AI-assisted development and LLM integration
  • Strong PHP and Laravel experience (5+ years)
  • Comfortable with Vue.js or willing to get there
  • Strong Architectural skills, planning for the future not just the present
  • Experience with APIs, integrations, and working with third-party systems
  • Familiarity with AWS or similar cloud environments

Mindset:

  • You take ownership. When something needs doing, you do it.
  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. We're building the plane while flying it, you won't always have a spec.
  • You communicate clearly. We're a remote team, writing well and speaking up matters.
  • You care about quality but also about shipping. Pragmatism over perfectionism.

What we offer

  • Fully remote (UK-based)
  • 25 days holiday
  • Contributory pension
  • Private healthcare
  • Death in service insurance
  • AIG Smart Health app

Who this probably isn't for

If you want a role where requirements are handed to you fully formed, tickets are perfectly groomed, and you can work in isolation, this won't suit you.

If you're energised by building something that matters, working closely with a team that gives a damn, and seeing your work go live and make a difference, let's talk.

Apply now — or reach out if you want to chat first.

We are committed to making reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process and welcome applications from all candidates.

To help ensure the recruitment process is accessible and that you can participate fully, please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments, equipment, software, or support for the interview, or if you are successful, for the role. As an equal opportunities employer, we will consider any such requests and discuss them with you as needed.

For context, the role operates between 8am and 5pm, Monday to Friday. The earlier start allows time to prepare before client communications begin and to participate in internal support and team discussions.

Client-facing communication is managed within structured timeframes during the day, which helps protect your time, reduce interruptions, and manage client expectations effectively.

The role also involves speaking with clients over Teams using video as part of delivering our service. If there are any practical issues with this or the way the role is structured, please let us know.

Technical Lead (PHP / Laravel)

Whiteley, Hampshire · Hybrid: Tue–Thu in the office, Mon and Fri from home · Permanent · Competitive salary

About us

WeBuyAnyPhone.com is the UK’s largest independent tech recycling business. We buy, refurbish and resell mobile phones, tablets, wearables and consoles, with every device tested, graded and repaired through our own operation in Whiteley. Much of that operation runs on software we’ve built in-house.

That software has scaled with the business, and we’re now investing in its future. We’ve completed a full review of our current platforms and developed a detailed proposal for what comes next.

We’re looking for an experienced Technical Lead to assess that proposal, set the technical direction, and lead the build through to launch and beyond.

The role

You’ll own our core technology. First, you’ll get under the skin of what we run today and what’s been proposed, then recommend the right path to the leadership team. Then you’ll lead the build, the migration and the running of it.

You report to the Head of Operations, who sets what the business needs its systems to do. You bring the technical experience that shapes how we get there, and you’ll have a real say in the direction itself. You own how it’s built, and you build it: hands-on, day to day, alongside our Senior Developer.

What you’ll do

  • Review our current platforms, the work done so far and the proposed direction. Recommend the way forward, with evidence, to the leadership team.
  • Own the architecture, code review, releases.
  • Take the chosen platform to production: hosting, single sign-on, CI/CD, monitoring and security testing.
  • Lead the migration off our current systems, through real-data rehearsals to a planned cutover in 2027.
  • Build the integrations: device diagnostics, couriers, payments and Open Banking, sales channels and accounting.
  • Work with the operations, finance, commercial and customer leads to turn business rules into system behaviour.
  • Keep everything documented and audit-ready.
  • Stay hands-on. Expect to spend about two-thirds of your time building.
  • AI is central to how we work. You’ll use tools like Claude Code daily to design, write, test and review. We’re looking for someone who directs AI to do the heavy lifting and owns what it produces. If you’d rather write it all by hand, this isn’t the role.

What you’ll bring

  • Full-stack Laravel: expert PHP (Laravel 11+ preferred; strong Symfony considered), strong relational databases (PostgreSQL preferred), and comfortable building server-rendered interfaces (Livewire, Blade or similar). Experienced in automated testing and static analysis (Pest or PHPUnit, PHPStan), and in designing and securing APIs.
  • Experience assessing an inherited system and making a clear, evidenced recommendation on its future.
  • Experience as a hands-on lead of a small development team.
  • At least one legacy-to-new platform migration taken live, including the data.
  • Daily, productive use of AI coding tools, and the judgement to review and own AI-written code.
  • Production ownership: Linux hosting (cloud or VPS), queues, CI/CD, monitoring and incident response.
  • Security by default: authentication and authorisation, secrets management, encryption and GDPR-aware data handling.
  • The ability to explain trade-offs plainly to non-technical directors, and to say no when it matters.

Nice to have

  • You’ve built inventory, warehouse management or order-fulfilment software: stock, locations, picking and despatch.
  • E-commerce or recommerce platforms, ideally with marketplace integrations.
  • Event-sourced or ledger-based data models, with audit trails and reporting built in.
  • Payments, Open Banking or courier API integrations.
  • Migrating data out of a document database such as MongoDB into a relational model.
  • Upgrading and stabilising older Laravel and livewire codebases while they’re in production.
  • Software that works with hardware on a busy floor: barcode scanners, label printers, device diagnostics.
  • Integrating third-party inventory, accounting and helpdesk platforms.
  • Reading and reviewing Python services (AI, data).

Why join

  • This is a building role, not a maintenance role. You won’t be babysitting someone else’s legacy. You’ll design, build and launch the platform the business runs on, and see the impact on the business every day.
  • You’ll shape a business’s core platform at a turning point, with board backing.
  • Real ownership: the technical direction, the standards and the team.
  • An AI-first engineering culture, backed from the top.
  • A visible outcome: every phone we buy, test and sell runs through what you build.
  • Work at the intersection of tech, sustainability and the circular economy, at an award-winning business (Sustainability and Environment, 2024 Mobile News Awards).
  • Company pension, gym membership, employee discount and a referral programme.
  • Casual dress, monthly recognition awards, an annual Summer of Fun, quarterly food vans and social events through the year.

How we hire

A short call, a practical exercise that you present back to us, then an in-person interview in Whiteley. We aim to complete the process within three weeks of your first call. We welcome applications from everyone and are happy to make reasonable adjustments during the process. Just let us know what you need.

To apply, send your CV and a few lines on a system you took live, what it delivered and how AI tools fit into the way you work. Full-time and permanent; you must have the right to work in the UK.

  • Do you have expert-level commercial experience with PHP using Laravel (11+ preferred) or Symfony?

  • Do you have hands-on experience with automated testing and static analysis (Pest or PHPUnit, PHPStan) and with designing and securing APIs?

jobs.title: Automated Quality Engineer - Contractor Role
jobs.description:
Job Introduction

At Tribepad, we put People first, Product second and Profit third. Our recruitment technology is used by employers such as Greggs, Northumberland County Council, the Met Office and DFS.

We're on a mission to make recruitment faster, fairer and better for everyone. Along the way, we've earned these accreditations:

  • Certified B Corporation

  • ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 27001 certified

The Role

Six-month Contractor role, full-time from January 2027, reporting to the CPTO.

Mostly remote - Sheffield two or three days a month for planning and team days. Standard day rate, paid monthly.

We’re moving quality from a manual, end-of-process activity to something built into the pipeline from the start. This is a hands-on role; you’ll define the quality strategy, build the automation foundations and get them running in CI, and bring our QA engineers and developers with you so the capability is theirs when you leave.

What you'll do

By the end of six months, we expect:

  • A written quality strategy for what the teams actually use: what we automate and at which layer, what stays exploratory, how we test AI-driven features, what the definition of done requires, and how quality is measured. Agreed with the product managers and the principal engineers.

  • Automated test foundations in place and running in CI on every merge: a

  • maintainable end-to-end suite in Playwright covering the critical recruiter and candidate journeys, API and contract tests for the backend, and a sensible approach to test data across tenants.

  • Quality shifted left. Testable acceptance criteria written with the product managers before work starts, developers writing and owning tests as part of the definition of done, QA pairing with developers from the first day of a ticket rather than at the end.

  • An approach to testing AI features: evaluation sets, golden questions, regression on model or prompt changes, and clear rules for when a non-deterministic output is good enough to ship.

  • AI used in the quality process itself. Test generation, coverage analysis, triage of failures and review automation, with judgement about where it helps and where it does not. Our developers are already using Claude heavily, and the quality practice should match.

  • Quality is visible in the delivery metrics: escaped defects, change failure rate, flaky test rate and time spent in test, feeding the delivery dashboard the leadership team already uses.

  • Our QA engineers own the automation: writing and maintaining Playwright and API tests, working in the pipeline and using AI tooling well. Built through pairing, code review and real tickets.

Before you apply:

  • You are available full-time from 1 January 2027 for six months, no overlapping contracts.

  • Operating through a limited company and set up to work outside IR35: own kit, own methods, substitution clause acceptable.

  • UK-based with the right to work, able to get to Sheffield two or three days a month and work UK hours.

  • Has built an automated test practice from a low base at least once, in a product team, and can show what it looked like six months after they left. Maintaining a suite someone else built does not count.

  • Has taken manual testers into automation before and can point to someone who got there because of it.

  • References from a product or engineering team they were embedded in, not just an agency or consultancy client.

Experience:

  • Extensive experience in software testing and leading quality engineering in a B2B SaaS product team working in sprints with CI/CD.

  • Playwright in-depth. Page object or fixture-based architecture, parallelism, handling flakiness properly rather than with retries, visual and accessibility checks, running in CI with useful reporting.

  • API and contract testing. REST APIs, schema and contract tests, test data setup and teardown, testing against a multi-tenant database without leaking between tenants.

  • Test strategy and risk-based design. Knowing what to automate at which layer, what to leave exploratory, and what not to test. Writing acceptance criteria with product managers that are testable from the start.

  • CI/CD and engineering fluency. Git, PRs, pipelines (GitHub Actions or similar), trunk-based development and feature flags. Comfortable reading application code in a Laravel or similar PHP codebase and SQL against PostgreSQL.

  • Testing AI and LLM-driven features. Evaluation sets, golden question sets, measuring accuracy and regression when models or prompts change, deciding what good enough means for non-deterministic output.

  • Using AI in the testing process itself. Generating and maintaining tests with tools like Claude or Copilot, AI-assisted triage and review, and clear judgement about where it helps and where it produces plausible rubbish.

  • Shift-left ways of working. Has moved a team from QA at the end to quality built in, with developers owning tests as part of the definition of done.

  • Quality metrics. Has defined and reported escaped defects, change failure rate, flaky test rate and test cycle time, and used them to drive improvements.

Nice to have, not required

  • Performance and load testing (k6 or similar) for a multi-tenant SaaS platform.

  • Security testing basics and working alongside pen tests and ISO 27001 controls.

  • Accessibility testing to WCAG 2.2, which matters for a candidate-facing product.

  • Testing integrations: webhooks, third-party APIs, HR system connectors, SSO.

  • Recruitment or HR tech. Applicant tracking, candidate journeys, the quirks of requisitions versus openings versus jobs.

  • Testing migrations from a legacy product.

  • A PE-backed or scale-up environment.

How we work
Three cross-functional teams, each with a Senior Product Manager, engineers and shared QA, working in two-week sprints with a demo every fortnight. Trunk-based development, feature flags, deploy on merge.

You will work day-to-day with the principal engineers who own technical direction and with the QA engineers. You will make the calls on quality approach and tooling.

jobs.description:
Job Introduction

At Tribepad, we put People first, Product second and Profit third. Our recruitment technology is used by employers such as Greggs, Northumberland County Council, the Met Office and DFS.

We're on a mission to make recruitment faster, fairer and better for everyone. Along the way, we've earned these accreditations:

  • Certified B Corporation
  • ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 27001 certified

At Tribepad, we've created an inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, respected and able to be themselves.

We want every candidate to have a fair and positive recruitment experience. If you need any adjustments or additional support at any stage of the process, we're happy to help.

The role

We're building our new recruitment platform from the ground up, and we want a Senior Full Stack Developer to help shape it. It's a multi-tenant SaaS product that will run hiring for some of the UK's biggest employers, from the careers site a candidate lands on to the offer they accept.

You'll join our Attract team, which owns how employers bring candidates in: creating and advertising jobs, careers sites, employer brands and the application journey. Like all our product teams, it's small: a Senior Product Manager, a Principal Engineer, two developers and a designer. The whole team plans the work, then builds and ships it.

Our stack

  • Backend: PHP 8 and Laravel (Octane, Horizon, Reverb), with Pest and PHPStan.
  • Frontend: React, Next.js and TypeScript in an Nx monorepo.
  • Data: PostgreSQL.
  • Platform: AWS, infrastructure as code, GitHub Actions, and a preview environment for every pull request.
  • Observability: OpenTelemetry and Grafana.

What you'll do

  • Build features end to end, from the database schema and API to the screens recruiters and candidates use.
  • Work with product and design to define the work before it's built: challenge requirements, spot risks early, and split work into small slices that can ship on their own.
  • Model a complex domain clearly. Recruitment has a lot of rules, and we use domain-driven design to keep them understandable.
  • Ship small, frequent changes behind feature flags, with tests, static analysis and code review, each one checked in its own preview environment before it merges.
  • Own what you ship in production: instrument it, watch how it behaves, and fix it if it breaks.
  • Build careers sites and application journeys that are fast, accessible and easy to find, along with the APIs and integrations that customers and partners rely on.
  • Review code, mentor other developers and help raise the bar for the whole team.
  • Use Claude Code as part of your everyday toolkit. Everything it produces goes through the same code review, tests and static analysis as any other change.

About you

  • A strong track record building production web applications in modern PHP 8 and Laravel.
  • Strong TypeScript and React, ideally with Next.js, and solid JavaScript fundamentals.
  • Relational database design and SQL, ideally PostgreSQL, including indexing and query performance.
  • Experience with multi-tenant SaaS or other high-volume systems: queues, caching, background jobs and concurrency.
  • TDD in practice, not just in theory.
  • A good working knowledge of domain-driven design.
  • Experience designing and versioning REST APIs.
  • Clear communication with product, design and QA, and good judgement about when to ask and when to decide.

Nice to have

  • AWS, infrastructure as code and CI/CD pipelines.
  • End-to-end testing with Playwright or similar.
  • Accessibility (WCAG), SEO and web performance.
  • Developing with AI coding tools such as Claude Code.
  • Building features with LLM APIs.
  • Integrations with job boards and other third-party APIs.
  • Recruitment or HR technology.

If you don't tick every box but this sounds like you, we'd still like to hear from you.

How we hire

Our process has two stages.

  • Get to know you: an initial meeting to talk about your experience and what you're looking for, and to tell you more about the role and the team.
  • In-person meeting: a face-to-face meeting of around 90 minutes, including a more technical conversation.

Created by landlords, for landlords, it offers investors everything they need to run a successful and compliant lettings business, whether they are full-time property professionals running large portfolios or accidental landlords with a single let.

A dynamic and fast-paced organisation, the NRLA is a great place to work, and it is not just us saying that, we have Investors in People Gold status to prove it. The association was also named one of the best companies to work for in the UK in a list compiled by The Sunday Times.

Our enthusiastic and ambitious staff work out of offices in Central Manchester and Central London with hybrid working options available. Colleagues typically work from home four days a week with one day in the office.

We are looking for colleagues who are professional, adaptable, and innovative. In return we offer an inclusive and creative working environment with attractive options for training and career development and a competitive salary and benefits package.

The NRLA package:

25 days annual leave increasing to 26 days with three years’ service, 27 days with five years’ service and 28 days with seven years’ service

Additional annual day off for your birthday

Salary exchange Pension scheme

Life assurance

Cash plan health and wellbeing benefit including Employee Assistance Programme and counselling service

Sick pay

Cycle purchase loans, season tickets loans and interest-free staff loans

Complimentary NRLA membership

Non-contractual annual performance-related bonus scheme

Enhanced maternity and paternity pay

Location:

London – Hybrid

Key Working Relationships:

  • Developers and QA specialists in every NRLA development team, including teams that join through acquisition from the date they transfer.
  • Head of Product Development, who owns the four key delivery metrics this role exists to move.
  • DevOps Manager, who owns the cloud platform, environments and runners the pipelines depend on.
  • Chief Technology Officer, as Data Protection Manager, for the data-handling terms of AI tools.
  • Product Directorate and Business Analysts, for documenting the domain knowledge that AI tools need.

Main Purpose and Scope of Job:

  • Increase the throughput and reliability of the NRLA development function by building the engineering platform that lets every team deliver small changes safely and often: AI-assisted development with clear guardrails, automated testing at every level and continuous integration and deployment pipelines for every product.
  • The role is an enabling role in the Team Topologies sense. It does not deliver features and it does not take work off teams indefinitely. It works alongside each team for a defined period, builds the capability with them, hands it over and moves on. Success is measured by the four key delivery metrics moving per product, by the review queue shrinking and by teams owning the practices without further help.

Duties and Key Responsibilities

AI-Assisted Development:

  • Own and maintain the AI-assisted development working agreement: approved tools, what may be shared, review expectations and how agent context is documented. Review it quarterly with the team.
  • Evaluate AI coding, review and testing tools against NRLA needs, run time-boxed trials, and recommend what to adopt, what to drop and what the budget should be.
  • Design the agent context files, prompts and workflows for each repository with the team that owns it, and keep them in version control alongside the code.
  • Work with Product and the BAs to get the domain knowledge that AI tools depend on out of people’s heads and into documentation that agents and new joiners can use.
  • Coach developers and QA in prompting, supervising and evaluating AI-generated code, and in designing software that AI tools can work on safely.
  • Measure the effect of AI tooling on the four key metrics and on quality, and report it to the Deputy Director monthly.

Test Automation:

  • Design the test automation strategy for each product with its team: unit, integration, contract and end-to-end tests, and the test data management that lets them run reliably on every change.
  • Build the first automated test suites and CI test stages with the team, then hand over ownership. Use AI tooling to generate and maintain tests where it is reliable, and say where it is not.
  • Work with the QA specialists to move testing earlier in the development cycle and to reduce manual regression testing before release.
  • Agree a definition of done that includes automated tests, and help teams meet it.

CI/CD Pipelines:

  • Design and build the continuous integration and deployment pipelines for every NRLA product, so that each change is built, tested and scanned automatically and releasing to production is a merge or a single action.
  • Agree with the DevOps Manager which environments, runners and infrastructure services the pipelines depend on, and who provides them.
  • Build dependency scanning, secrets detection, licence checks and static analysis into the pipeline, and set the observability minimums (logging, monitoring, alerting, error-to-ticket flow) for each product.
  • Remove the manual steps between a change being finished and being live, and measure the lead time that results.

Enablement and Handover:

  • Work with one or two teams at a time for an agreed period, in the facilitating interaction mode, with a written statement of what capability the team will own at the end and a date.
  • Run the standing AI and engineering practice slot at the fortnightly engineering community session.
  • Support the integration of acquired development teams by bringing their codebases onto the same pipelines, test standards and AI working agreement from their first quarter.
  • Document everything built so that no pipeline, test suite or tool depends on this role to keep running.

Delivery Performance:

  • Help the Deputy Director baseline the four key delivery metrics per product in October 2026 and automate their collection from Git, CI and Jira.
  • Analyse where time goes between a change being written and being live, and propose the improvements with the largest payback for each team.
  • Protect the review queue: track pull request size and review turnaround, and work with teams to keep both within the agreed norms.

Security, Data Protection and Compliance:

  • Apply NRLA’s information governance standards to every tool and pipeline, and raise data protection questions with the CTO before, not after, a tool is used.
  • Comply with NRLA policy and statutory requirements, including data protection, information security, equality and diversity, health and safety and the code of conduct.

Person Specification

Qualifications:

  • Degree in computer science, engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Cloud (GCP), DevOps or security certifications (desirable).

Skills and Abilities:

  • Uses AI coding assistants and agentic tools well on real codebases, understands their limits, and can set guardrails others will follow.
  • Designs and builds CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions or similar) and automated test suites, and coaches developers to own them.
  • Explains technical choices to developers, QA, product managers and senior leaders without line authority, and brings people with them.
  • Works with one team at a time to a defined handover, resists becoming the permanent owner of what has been built, and documents as it goes.
  • Measures the effect of a change rather than asserting it, and changes course when the data says so.

Experience:

  • At least four years of professional software development, including hands-on CI/CD, test automation and DevOps work on production systems.
  • Has introduced AI-assisted development tools into a team’s day-to-day work and can describe the results, including what did not work.
  • Has built or substantially improved automated test coverage and deployment pipelines for an existing codebase.

About Broadband Genie

Broadband Genie has been helping people compare and switch broadband since 2008. Our mission is to take the stress out of switching for the thousands of customers who use us every year.

We’re a team of 13 across product, acquisition and commercial, working cross-functionally so our focus stays on making the website better for customers. You’d join the product team, currently five people. We value open, transparent communication and real collaboration, and in a team this size the work you ship is visible and makes a difference.

The role

You’ll design and build the technology that moves our product forward and solves real business problems.

The role has a backend focus. Most of your time will go on the systems behind the site: our PHP/Symfony platform, the data and integrations that power our comparison results, our partner and affiliate connections, and the AWS infrastructure it all runs on.

Frontend skills are a real plus. You’ll pick up frontend work when the team needs it, and we’re moving our frontend toward Stimulus and React, so experience there is especially welcome.

It’s a small team, so you’ll have a direct impact on the product and the growth of the business. We’re looking for someone who enjoys working with pace, focus and flexibility.

What you’ll do

Own and develop our backend systems

  • Design, build and maintain backend features on our PHP/Symfony platform, including our in-house CMS and admin tools

  • Build and maintain integrations with third-party APIs and data feeds: broadband availability data, provider products and deals, affiliate networks (such as Awin and Impact) and ad platforms (such as Google Ads, Microsoft Advertising and Meta)

  • Develop and support our partner API, including the endpoints, reporting and data-passing our partners rely on

  • Keep the data behind our comparison results accurate and reliable, from availability lookups and product data to lead and sales imports

Shape the product with the team

  • Find and adopt new tools and practices, including AI-assisted development, that help the product succeed long term

  • Work closely with commercial and marketing colleagues on things like onboarding new providers and partners, and tracking and campaign changes

  • Pick up frontend work when needed, alongside our frontend developer

  • Join our weekly team check-ins, monthly product updates and monthly in-person meetups in Cambridge (attendance expected, travel costs covered)

What you’ll bring

Essential

  • 3+ years’ commercial experience as a backend or full stack developer

  • Significant experience on professional websites with complex data feeds and third-party integrations

  • Strong object-oriented PHP (8.x), with a solid grasp of the language beyond frameworks such as Symfony or Laravel

  • MySQL database design, query optimisation and administration

  • Designing, building and consuming REST APIs, including authentication and webhooks

  • Cloud infrastructure, ideally AWS, plus Docker, infrastructure as code (Terraform) and CI/CD

  • Git, including pull-request based code review

  • Automated testing (for example PHPUnit)

  • Secure coding practices and handling personal data in line with UK GDPR

Nice to have

  • Responsive, accessible HTML and CSS (Sass), built with a high degree of visual accuracy

  • Modern JavaScript, including Stimulus or React (the frameworks we’re moving toward), and build tooling such as Vite

  • Site performance and accessibility standards (Core Web Vitals, WCAG)

  • Data warehousing and reporting tools, especially dbt (plus Redshift and QuickSight)

  • Product analytics and conversion tracking (for example PostHog, Google Tag Manager and server-side conversion APIs)

  • Using AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code or GitHub Copilot effectively and responsibly

  • Experience in comparison, affiliate or lead-generation businesses

Don’t tick every box? If you’re close and the role excites you, we’d still like to hear from you.

Our tech stack

  • Backend: PHP 8, Symfony, MySQL, REST APIs, PHPUnit

  • Infrastructure: AWS (ECS, RDS), Docker, Terraform, CI/CD, Cloudflare

  • Data and analytics: Redshift, dbt, QuickSight, PostHog

  • Frontend: HTML, Sass, JavaScript, Vite, moving toward Stimulus and React

  • Tools and workflow: Git, Shortcut, Slack, AI-assisted development

Our hiring process

  • Intro call. A short video call about the role, the team and what you’re looking for.

  • Exercise. A practical exercise based on the kind of work you’d do here. We’re flexible on timing, so fit it around your week.

What we offer

Genie is Great Place To Work certified, and listed among the Best Workplaces in Advertising, Media and Marketing.

  • Flexible working: flexible working options in a distributed team

  • Time off: 25 days’ annual leave plus bank holidays, and your birthday off

  • Salary exchange schemes: electric car and Cycle to Work schemes

jobs.description:
About the company

Who are OnCommerce?


OnCommerce is a global selling platform that powers a growing network of retail channels, including:

  • OnBuy - The only marketplace in the world to give customers instant Cashback on everything
  • easyShop - An all-new marketplace created in collaboration with the easy® family of brands
  • Comet - The iconic UK tech brand making its return later this year


OnCommerce is growing fast, launching new brands and scaling to power the future of ecommerce.


Be Part of the Story

OnCommerce is constantly evolving. Everyone here plays a hands-on role in shaping what comes next, building brands that make an impact across global markets. There’s no red tape or rigid corporate structure; just smart people taking ownership and figuring things out as we build something big together. The pace is fast, priorities shift, things aren’t always perfectly set up, and you’ll often need to get stuck in and solve problems. But if you thrive in that kind of environment, you’ll have real influence, real ownership, and the chance to grow with a rapidly scaling business.

About the role

The Head of Platform Engineering is accountable for translating the technology strategy into high-performing engineering teams and a reliable, secure and scalable platform. The role owns engineering-wide delivery performance, capability, standards and operational resilience across the current platform and target state. It ensures transformation activity progresses without compromising live trading, customer experience or essential service operations. The role leads the adoption of AI as a core part of the software development lifecycle (SDLC) and thedaily work of every engineer and engineering team. It ensures AI is used to improve speed, quality and reliability, and is used safely, cost-effectively and for the right reasons.

The Head of Platform Engineering leads through the Engineering Lead/s, creates consistency across squads and provides the CTO with clear visibility of engineering performance, capacity, risk, AI adoption and investment needs.

Key accountabilities

  • Convert the CTO's strategy and architectural direction into an engineering plan, capability model and practical operating rhythm.
  • Define clear ownership across engineering domains, squads, services and support responsibilities.
  • Recommend changes to team structure, sourcing, capability and capacity based on delivery and platform needs, including the productivity gains enabled by AI.
  • Lead the strategy for AI-enabled engineering and make it the standard way of working across the function.

Engineering delivery

  • Own cross-team engineering delivery health, capacity planning, dependencies, risks and escalation.
  • Set expectations for measurable and increasingly predictable delivery, without reducing success to output or sprint completion alone.
  • Partner with Product leadership to ensure priorities are understood, technically feasible and matched to available engineering capacity.

AI-enabled engineering

  • Embed AI across every stage of the SDLC: discovery and requirements, design, coding, code review, testing, documentation, deployment, and incident investigation and response.
  • Make AI assistants and coding agents part of daily work for developers, quality engineers and platform engineers, with clear guidance on where they add most value.
  • Select, approve and manage the engineering AI toolset, including licences, seats, access and integration with code repositories, pipelines and internal knowledge.
  • Own usage, quota and cost management for AI tools: set budgets and limits by team, monitor consumption, alert before quotas are hit and prevent wasteful or runaway usage.
  • Define and enforce acceptable use, covering approved tools, data classification, and keeping secrets, credentials, customer data and personal data out of prompts and context.
  • Ensure engineers remain accountable for all AI-generated output, which must meet the same review, testing and security standards as any other code.
  • Set guardrails for agentic AI, including scoped permissions, human approval for production-affecting actions and full auditability.
  • Build AI capability through training, playbooks, shared prompts and skills, and a network of AI champions.
  • Measure the impact of AI on delivery, quality and reliability, rather than usage alone, and act on the findings.

Platform health and operational resilience

  • Own the engineering operating model for live-service support, on-call coverage, incident escalation and service restoration.
  • Establish consistent expectations for observability, runbooks, service ownership and post-incident review.
  • Ensure recurring operational issues and root causes are addressed through prioritised engineering work, using AI to speed up diagnosis and analysis where appropriate.

Engineering standards and governance

  • Owns engineering standards and governance for design, coding, review, testing,documentation, deployment, maintainability and AI-assisted development within the CTO'sstrategic guardrails.
  • Create assurance that standards are being applied across current and future platforms.
  • Enable Engineering Leads and senior engineers to contribute to and improve shared standards.

Architecture and technical decision-making

  • Govern platform-wide engineering decisions and ensure squad designs remain aligned withagreed architecture.
  • Own the engineering implications of coexistence and migration between legacy andtarget-state platforms.
  • Escalate enterprise architecture, material investment and risk-acceptance decisions to the CTO, while retaining authority for routine engineering decisions.

People, capability and culture

  • Lead, coach and performance-manage Engineering Leads and designated senior engineering roles.
  • Own engineering workforce planning, capability assessment, succession, hiring standards and leadership development, including AI skills in hiring and development frameworks.
  • Calibrate performance and career expectations across squads, working with the People team.
  • Build a culture of accountability, psychological safety, constructive challenge, blameless learning and responsible experimentation with AI.

Security, quality and technical debt

  • Embed secure engineering, automated testing and quality controls into engineering ways ofworking and definitions of done.
  • Manage AI-specific risks, including insecure or unlicensed generated code, data leakage, prompt injection and over-reliance on unreviewed output, working with Security.
  • Maintain engineering-wide visibility of technical debt, operational risk and remediation priorities.
  • Present material trade-offs in business terms and escalate decisions beyond delegated risk or investment authority.

Governance and communication

  • Provide the CTO with clear reporting on delivery, platform health, capability, quality, risk, transformation progress, and AI adoption, usage, spend and value.
  • Ensure material cross-team blockers and trade-offs are surfaced early with recommended actions.
  • Maintain constructive relationships with Product, Data, Security, Tech Operations and commercial stakeholders.

Authority

  • Define and implement engineering standards and operating practices within CTO-approved principles.
  • Allocate engineering capacity between squads within the agreed portfolio and budget.
  • Approve routine cross-team technical and delivery decisions.
  • Approve engineering AI tools and set usage limits, quotas and budgets within the agreed AI policy and budget.
  • Restrict or withdraw access to AI tools where use breaches policy or creates security, data or cost risk.
  • Require remediation where services, practices or delivery fall below agreed standards.
  • Pause or restrict engineering changes presenting unacceptable immediate operational or

security risk, escalating material impact to the CTO.

  • Escalate enterprise architecture, significant investment, strategic priority and risk-acceptance

decisions to the CTO.

Leadership expectations

  • Lead the function through Engineering Leads rather than taking over routine squad management.
  • Balance transformation pace with the stability and supportability of live services.
  • Model effective and responsible use of AI in own work and expect the same of leaders.
  • Make standards visible, measurable and proportionate.
  • Create clarity without unnecessary central approval or bureaucracy.
  • Address underperformance, capacity constraints and capability gaps directly and fairly.
  • Represent engineering risks and trade-offs honestly to Product and executive stakeholders.


What We Are Looking For

Essential

  • Substantial engineering leadership experience across multiple teams in a product-led, marketplace, e-commerce or high-traffic environment.
  • Strong software engineering background with credibility across monolithic and service-based architectures.
  • Experience leading engineering transformation while keeping a live, revenue-generating platform operational.
  • Proven people leadership, including managing managers, workforce planning, hiring, performance and development.
  • Strong experience of cloud operations, service reliability, security engineering, incident management and technical debt governance.
  • Hands-on experience using AI coding assistants and agents, and of leading their adoption across engineering teams with measurable results.
  • Ability to establish engineering standards and improve cross-team delivery in a fast-moving, resource-constrained environment.

Desirable

  • Experience with PHP/Laravel, GCP, AWS, MySQL, Couchbase or MongoDB, Redis, APIs and event-driven systems.
  • Experience of composable or MACH-oriented migration on a live platform.
  • Experience managing blended permanent, partner, nearshore or offshore engineering teams.
  • Breadth across modern service technologies such as Node.js, Go or Python.
  • Experience of AI governance, including usage and cost controls, acceptable-use policies and secure integration of AI tools into the SDLC


Salary and Benefits

The salary on offer for this role is upto £120,000 dependent on experience.

We also offer the following benefits:

  • Company Equity - In return for helping us to grow, we will offer you significant company equity, meaning you own a piece of the business we are all working so hard to build.
  • 25 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays
  • 1 extra day off for your birthday
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Perks at Work benefit platform
  • Opportunities for career development and progression


Location

This is a hybrid role, with a minimum of three days a week in one of our offices in Manchester or Bournemouth.


By submitting this application, I agree that my personal data will be collected, processed, and retained by the company solely for the purposes of managing and assessing my candidacy.


Our Commitment

OnCommerce is an equal opportunities employer. We are dedicated to creating a fair and transparent workforce, starting with a recruitment process that does not discriminate on the basis of gender, sexual orientation, marital or civil partnership status, pregnancy or maternity, gender reassignment, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief, disability, or age.


Just a heads up — we never use WhatsApp or any messaging apps to contact candidates. If someone reaches out this way, it isn’t us and let the recruitment team know.

jobs.description:
STRICTLY NO AGENCIES. We are only accepting direct applications for this role. Any unsolicited CVs sent will be treated as a gift and will not be subject to any terms or fees. RECRUITERS: please do not call or email us regarding this role.

HYBRID: THREE DAYS A WEEK IN OUR FARRINGDON, LONDON OFFICE

Stack: Next.js, React and TypeScript on the front end. Laravel and PHP on the back end. A legacy PHP and CodeIgniter platform being modernised alongside it. AWS underneath. Claude Code used throughout engineering.

About Eventogy

Eventogy Ltd is a UK event management SaaS company based in Farringdon, London. Twenty years old, profitable, privately held. Our clients are large international enterprises in regulated sectors: Deutsche Bank, Santander, BNPP, Ford, Kia, Toyota, Linklaters, Clifford Chance and Freshfields among them. The bar for what we ship is set by those customers, not by us.

The role

You will own the engineering team's delivery, every day. What was promised lands, at the standard our clients expect, and problems surface at the start of the week, not the day before a deadline. The work is predominantly on our new platform, built on Next.js and Laravel. Our original PHP and CodeIgniter platform runs alongside it while clients move across.

Engineering is organised into two pods. Each pod is given its own features, epics and technical challenges, and each is led by a hands-on Principal Engineer who reports to you. You drive both pods, and the Principal Engineers are how you do it: each leads their pod technically and is accountable to you for its output. Together you form a small leadership trident, which you head, that owns the technical side of the platform and its delivery: architecture, platform, engineering standards and technical decisions. The Principal Engineers lead technical direction for the areas their pods own and keep both pods building the same way. You set the direction for both pods and the order of ownership and accountability, hold each pod to its output, and make the call when the Principal Engineers cannot agree.

The lines are clear. The CTO sets technology strategy and security, and is ultimately accountable for the platform. The Product Owner owns what gets built. The Delivery Manager owns the plan and its timelines, manages stakeholders, and is the team's voice to the rest of the business. You own the technical delivery behind all of it, and the technical operation of the platform in production. You are the critical path: every date the Delivery Manager communicates is one you are accountable for engineering to hit. You report to the CTO and work directly with the CEO on delivery.

That makes your partnership with the Delivery Manager the centre of the job. You size work with the Product Owner and Delivery Manager before it is committed, so the dates that go out are ones the team can hit. You give the Delivery Manager an honest, early read on progress and risk, so the business hears about a problem while there is still time to act on it. Then you make the dates happen. You will be measured on delivery outcomes.

We work on a simple principle: build it, run it, own it. The engineers who write a feature are the ones who deploy it, support it in production and answer for how it performs. You will embed that across the team, and it starts with you: this role owns the whole of the technical delivery, not just the plan.

This is a hands-on role. Expect to spend 20 to 30 percent of your time writing code: enough to stay credible with the team and close to the codebase, not so much that you disappear into it.

It is not a role for someone who wants to keep a calendar and report status upwards. It is for someone who takes delivery personally: who steps in, unblocks, re-plans and keeps pushing until the work is live.

What you will do

  • Drive both pods day to day, through the two Principal Engineers. Know where every piece of work stands, and challenge it when a task has taken far longer than it should
  • Head the leadership trident with the two Principal Engineers: agree and write down the decisions on architecture, platform and standards, and settle technical disagreements between the pods
  • Size work with the Product Owner and Delivery Manager before it is committed, in enough detail to plan against and to give clients dates
  • Work hand in hand with the Delivery Manager: she owns the plan and the stakeholder conversation, you own the engineering behind it, including dependencies, technical risk and team capacity
  • Raise slippage with the Delivery Manager early and honestly, with a recovery plan attached, so she can manage expectations before a date is missed
  • Own the delivery numbers, work committed against work delivered and time from start to live, and report them weekly to the CTO and CEO
  • Make build it, run it, own it the way the team works: engineers take their work from ticket to production and stay accountable for it once it is live, with no handing problems over the wall
  • Own production across both platforms, including our original platform, and the on-call rota that supports it
  • Set, publish and enforce the engineering standard for code review, testing and releases through the trident, applied to everyone, and to AI-written code as much as human-written
  • Own people, performance, and pay and review conversations across both pods, drawing on each Principal Engineer's view of the engineers in their pod
  • Hire, onboard and performance-manage engineers, dealing with under-delivery directly and fairly and running formal processes properly when they are needed
  • Write code yourself for 20 to 30 percent of your time
  • Run a lean engineering rhythm: planning, stand-ups, reviews and retrospectives that earn their time

What success looks like at 90 days

  • Work delivered against work committed is measurably higher than when you arrived
  • The trident is running, with a written engineering standard published and applied to both pods
  • The quarter's committed work has landed as promised

Requirements


You have run engineering delivery before

  • At least four years leading software engineers in a technical delivery capacity, accountable for what shipped and when, not only for technical direction
  • You have led a team of five to ten engineers on a live SaaS product
  • A record of shipping committed work to agreed dates that you can talk through in specifics: what was promised, what landed, and what you did when it went wrong
  • You have taken an underperforming team up a level, and can say exactly what you changed and how

You estimate and plan seriously

  • You have built estimates other people relied on, and you can explain your method: decomposition, ranges, confidence and contingency
  • You measure how accurate your estimates turn out to be, and you improve them
  • You tell stakeholders bad news early, with a plan attached

You are hands-on in our stack

  • Current, hands-on skill with Next.js, React and TypeScript, and with Laravel and PHP. You can pick up a ticket yourself, not just review one
  • You already work AI-first: tools such as Claude Code are part of how you build every day, and you know where they help and where they hurt
  • Comfortable reading code, reviewing pull requests and challenging an estimate or a design on its technical merits
  • A working understanding of CI/CD, environments, releases and running production on AWS

You lead people well

  • Direct, fair and comfortable having hard conversations about performance
  • You have run formal performance processes properly, from the first conversation to the outcome
  • You have led through tech leads or principal engineers, giving them real technical ownership while holding them to account for their team's output
  • You build accountability in a team without micromanaging it
  • You have made engineers responsible for their work in production, not just for getting it merged, and can explain how you made that stick

Nice to have

  • Experience with regulated enterprise clients, such as banks or law firms
  • Modernising or migrating a legacy platform while still shipping on it
  • CodeIgniter or other legacy PHP frameworks
  • Event technology
  • Working under ISO 27001 or through client security reviews

This probably is not for you if

  • You see the job as running ceremonies and reporting status
  • You consider delivery someone else's problem once the estimate is agreed
  • You think production support belongs to a different team from the one that wrote the code
  • You would rather not report delivery numbers every week, good or bad
  • You want to stop writing code entirely, or to write code full time
  • You want a fixed routine and a clean finish at five o'clock whatever state the release is in
  • You are looking for a fully remote role

Benefits


How we work

  • A small, senior team where decisions are made quickly and you work closely with the CTO and CEO
  • Hybrid, three days a week in our Farringdon office. There is a good coffee shop next door and a food market outside
  • A bonus tied to delivery results
  • Company pension scheme
  • Gym membership
  • Multiple progression routes: leadership, product or deep technical
  • Serious investment in AI tooling and training

How to apply

Apply with your CV and answer both questions below on the application form. Applications without answers to both will not be reviewed.

  • Tell us about a delivery commitment that was at risk of slipping. How did you spot it, what did you do, and how did it end?
  • How do you build an estimate you would put your name to? Walk us through a real example, and tell us how close the outcome came.

We are an equal opportunities employer. You must be eligible to work in the UK without requiring sponsorship, hold a valid visa or UK residency, be currently based in the UK, and be prepared to undergo high-level security clearance.

NO AGENCIES.
